feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is the baseline (iteration 0, reproduced in iteration 9): the oval finished 20/20 at about 1.65 s, and the s-bend and slalom went off track at progress about 0.17 and 0.12. Every change from it has failed. Sensor lead at y = 0.03 and 0.07 m collapsed the oval (iterations 3 and 4). Footprints of 8 and 16 mm did too (iterations 5 and 6). The wider +/-0.032 m array collapsed it at 0.6 kg (iteration 7), which overturns the earlier bend-gain reading from iteration 2. Body length 0.12 m collapsed it (iteration 8). Mass 0.7 kg cut finishes to 6/20 (iteration 10), which refutes the damping idea. The Integrator kept the controller unchanged, so the geometry is the only variable. This is the last iteration, so no further race can use these requests. They are given for the record: if the unseen track is bend-heavy and the oval holds, the bend limit is most likely controller-side and not fixable by geometry. Keep the baseline as the reference.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_positions at x = 0, +/-0.012, +/-0.024 m with y = 0.05 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body_length 0.16 m and mass 0.6 kg. Iterations 3 to 10 show that changing any of these alone collapses or cuts the oval finish rate.
If the next race shows the oval finishing 20/20 at about 1.65 s with a score near 356, treat the baseline as robust and make no geometry change, since the unseen track is scored on this platform.

If the next race shows line loss at the bends with outer sensors near 0 and max_error near 0.06 m, record the bend limit as controller-side (kp, kd or base_speed) for future work, and do not widen the array, since iterations 1, 2 and 7 showed that the spread change cut the oval.
